title: Capacity preflight sync: GPU pairing notes
content:
Purpose / context:
- Prep for 1:1 with Alejandro on Tues. Primary goal: align on Q2 reservation posture for Dedicated GPU pools and confirm short runway actions for the upcoming product beta (mid-March).
- This is a quick personal prep doc — shorthand, hypotheses, and required asks to get a decision (or a clear follow-up).

Timebox (30m total):
- 5m: status recap (current commitments, utilization, high-risk queues)
- 10m: present demand scenarios + recommendation
- 10m: tradeoffs, autoscale/cost mitigations, decision or next steps
- 5m: assign owners and dates

Quick facts (snapshot):
- Committed capacity: 320 A100e-equivalent GPUs across 3 pools (prod, staging, burst).
- Average 7d utilization (tokens/sec normalized): 68% overall; prod pool 74% at peak hours (14:00-18:00 PT).
- Current burst policy: allow 20% overcommit (soft), enforced by quota guardrails.
- Open dedicated requests: two medium customers (est. 12 GPUs combined) slated for late March.
- Upcoming internal beta (product feature X) forecasted traffic +30–45% during first 6 weeks based on load tests.

Hypotheses to test / things to highlight:
1) The prod pool has <12% headroom in peak windows -> higher risk of degraded latency under beta launch spike.
2) Autoscale alone will not prevent token latency regression because cold-starts and placement jitter add tail latency spikes.
3) Short-term reservation increase (one commit bump, ~32 GPUs) is cost-effective vs. emergency burst capacity at 2.5x price if we hit throttling.

Demand scenarios (3):
- Conservative (baseline): +10% traffic; autoscale handles it; no reservation change; monitor.
- Likely (planning): +30% traffic first 4 weeks then back to +15%; recommend +32 GPUs reserved for Q2 (staggered allocation: 16 to prod, 8 staging, 8 burst).
- Extreme (risk): +60% traffic if beta goes viral; need rapid burst policy + regional fallback to avoid user-visible errors. Escalation runbook required.

Quick math for likely scenario (back-of-envelope):
- Prod pool current A100-eq: 200 GPUs, peak utilization 74% -> effectively 52 available headroom at peak. +30% load increases token demand ~= need for additional ~60 GPUs during peak.
- Reserve recommendation: +32 GPUs reduces probability of hitting >90% utilization by ~50% (based on previous queuing sims). Remaining delta handled by short burst and routing to warmed fallback model.

Tradeoffs & mitigations to propose (talk track):
- Upside: reservation reduces tail latency risk, keeps SLA for paying customers, lower unit cost vs. on-demand burst.
- Downside: spend delta ~3–4% of quarterly infra budget if committed for full quarter. If adoption undershoots, we can scale down at quarter end.
- Mitigations: attach a usage commitment corridor (schedule review in 6 weeks), enable tighter autoscale cooldowns + pre-warming for top-10 routes, and add a canary-run to validate traffic shape before full beta release.

Questions to ask Alejandro (explicit ask list):
- Are we comfortable committing +32 GPUs now if we get sign-off? If not, what is the maximum upside we can accept for short-term burst cost?
- Should we prioritize reservation in us-west-2 or split regionally (us-west-2 + eu-west-1) given product beta audience?
- Any business tolerance for degraded latency during first 2 weeks (trade customer churn vs. cost)?
- Approve spending owner for emergency burst fund? (need name + limit)

Operational actions I will propose (assign during sync):
- Run a per-model token/sec projection for the beta (Evelyn) — due 2025-02-24. (Jira CAP-432)
- Create a temporary reservation PR (infra) with flags for rollback and region split (Jonas) — due 2025-02-25.
- Add a canary test run during off-peak with simulated beta traffic (me) — schedule Wed/Thu next week.
- Short doc for support on expected errors and escalation path (oncall) — draft by 2025-02-26.

Notes-to-self / conversation snippets to use:
- "We can buy latency insurance cheaply now; the question is whether we prefer cost predictability vs. risk appetite for potential user impact."
- "Autoscale is necessary but not sufficient; pre-warm and placement determinism matter more for tail latency."
- "If we commit, mark it as reversible and pair with a 6-week review clause."

Follow-ups (expected outcomes from meeting):
- Decision: approve +32 GPU reservation OR green-light 14-day increased burst budget + tighter observability.
- If reservation approved: Jonas to open infra PR and Evelyn to provide token/sec breakdown.
- If burst budget approved: define budget limit, owner, and telemetry checks; set auto-cutover to avoid runaway spend.

Rough backlog of tickets / reminders:
- CAP-432: beta token projections (linked above).
- CAP-437: autoscale cooldown tweaks (add 30s pre-warm + reduce scale-down aggressiveness).
- SUPPORT-1051: add buyer-facing note about possible degraded latency during early beta (customer comms draft).

Closing personal checklist for the 1:1:
- [ ] Print succinct one-pager of the numbers (1 page).
- [ ] Bring cost delta estimates for +16 / +32 / +64 GPUs.
- [ ] Prepare canary run schedule and min viable validation checks.
- [ ] Confirm who signs off on emergency burst spend.

Misc (random thoughts):
- If we add reserved GPUs, consider tagging them with "beta-prewarm" so usage attribution for charging is clear.
- Might be worth a small spike on placement determinism work (ticket CAP-460) — low effort, high ROI for tail latency.

Status: rough draft, will refine after 1:1 and update the Confluence planning doc.
